task.title: Relics: serve relic reads from the local index
task.description:
A relic is a new kind of record in Workbook, separate from tasks. It holds specs, plans, decisions, transcripts and similar material, with the same history and sharing that tasks have. A relic has a title, a type, an author, links, and content made of named parts.

This story puts relics in the local SQLite index so that reads are fast and do not walk Git history. Git stays the source of truth.

## What this delivers

- The index holds relics, their properties, parts with their fields and each body's format, size and object ID, and the list of recorded changes for each relic.
- `relic list` and `relic show` are served from the index.
- Body text is not copied into the index. It is read from Git by its object ID when it is shown, one direct read per body.
- The index is updated only for relics that changed, as for tasks today.
- The index can be deleted at any time and rebuilt from the refs. `workbook rebuild` covers relics.
- A stale or missing index is detected and repaired before a relic read answers, as it is for tasks.

## Rules that matter

- The index is disposable. Nothing may exist only there.
- Direct SQL writes stay unsupported.
- Leave room for links searchable by either end. The next story adds them.
- Building the index on a fresh clone must take seconds and never minutes. The benchmark story sets and measures the exact target (under 5 seconds for 1,000 relics, 20,000 parts and 10,000 links), so do not design anything here that makes it unreachable.

## Done when

- Deleting the index and rebuilding gives the same answers as before.
- The same relic history gives the same index contents whatever order the refs are read in.
- An interrupted update leaves an index that repairs itself.
- Several worktrees and several processes can read and update relics in one repository at once.
- Task commands are no slower with the relic tables present and empty.

## Not in this story

Links, schemas, history and diff commands, and the benchmark family.

## Where the design is

The approved design is "Workbook Relics Design" (2026-11-21). It is kept out of the repository. Until "Relics: teach agents to use relics and store the design as the first relic" is done, an untracked copy sits at `specs/2026-11-21-relics-design.html` in Dylan's checkout. After that, read the relic. This description carries what the story needs, and the design wins where the two disagree.
